# LoRa module and Meshtastic documents

Documents behind the LoRa side of the compute-module respin study (MESHSAT-709, appendix 32.35, `docs/respin-research-cm5-2026-09-04.md`): the Wio-SX1262 that PCB-B carries and the two Ebyte E22 modules that meshtasticd on the module would drive over SPI, with the Meshtastic pin templates and pages that describe that setup. Fetched 4 September 2026. The licence remark of the parent folder applies; the two YAML templates come from the Meshtastic firmware repository (GPL-3.0) and the page extracts from the project's documentation site. Nothing here has been built.

| File | Source | Date | What it is used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seeed-wio-sx1262-module-datasheet-v1.1.pdf` | https://files.seeedstudio.com/products/SenseCAP/Wio_SX1262/Wio-SX1262_Module_Datasheet.pdf | 4 Sep 2026 (V1.1) | the module PCB-B carries: pinout, RF and supply figures, the mechanical drawing (its STEP is in `../wio/`) |
| `ebyte-e22-900m22s-user-manual-en.pdf` | https://www.cdebyte.com/pdf-down.aspx?id=1822 | 4 Sep 2026 | the 22 dBm SX1262 module of the MeshAdv Mini: pinout, SPI and control lines, RF figures, footprint |
| `ebyte-e22-900m30s-user-manual-en-v1.20.pdf` | https://www.rcscomponents.kiev.ua/datasheets/e22-900m30s_usermanual_en_v1_20.pdf (distributor copy) | 4 Sep 2026 (v1.20) | the 30 dBm SX1262 module with PA and LNA of the MeshAdv-Pi: pinout, the RXEN and TXEN switching, current at full power, footprint |
| `lora-MeshAdv-900M30S.yaml`, `lora-MeshAdv-Mini-900M22S.yaml` | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshtastic/firmware/master/bin/config.d/lora-MeshAdv-900M30S.yaml and `.../lora-MeshAdv-Mini-900M22S.yaml` | 4 Sep 2026 | the meshtasticd config.d templates for the two modules on a Raspberry Pi header: CS, IRQ, Busy and Reset pins, the TXen and RXen lines (M30S) or DIO2 as the RF switch (M22S), DIO3 as the TCXO supply; the pin map a carrier of our own reproduces or replaces with a template of its own |
| `meshtastic-linux-native-devices-wayback-2024-09-06.md` | https://meshtastic.org/docs/hardware/devices/linux-native-hardware/ as archived by the Wayback Machine on 6 September 2024 (text extract; the live URL now lands on the meshtasticd overview page) | 4 Sep 2026 | the original Linux-native page: tested devices, the rule that only SPI radios work (no UART hats), config.yaml, the SPI overlay, GPS over UART, the systemd unit |
